name: veterinary_clinic_system_018_boarding_overstay_flag
instruction:
Flag every boarding overstay and notify the owners at the episode close.

A reservation is an overstay if and only if its status is 'checked_in' and check_out is strictly before the episode date (check_out == episode_date is NOT an overstay).

For each overstay:
1. Set the reservation status to 'overstay' and set overstay_days = (episode_date - check_out) whole days.
2. Free the assigned run: set the corresponding boarding_runs status to 'available' and current_patient_id to empty.
3. Push a communications row to the owner: channel='email', direction='outbound', subject='Overstay notice <batch_code>', body='<patient_name> (reservation <reservation_id>) was scheduled to check out on <check_out> and is still on the books as of <episode_date> — <overstay_days> day(s) overdue. Please contact the front desk.', logged_by='system', occurred_at=<episode_date with time>, owner_id, patient_id, reservation_id, batch_code. Skip if a communication with this subject and (patient_id, reservation_id) already exists for this batch.
4. Push an audit_log entry with action='OVERSTAY_FLAGGED', actor='system', actor_role='front_desk', target_collection='boarding_reservations', target_id=<reservation_id>, details='Overstay flagged for reservation <reservation_id>: <overstay_days> days, batch <batch_code>', occurred_at=<episode_date with time>, batch_code.

Finally, create exactly one ops_reports row 'boarding_overstay_summary' keyed by the live batch_code with: episode_date, overstay_count, total_overstay_days, by_run_type (dict {run_type: count}), by_location (dict {location_name: count}), by_species (dict {species: count}), and communications_count. Overwrite any existing row for this batch.

Do not touch reservations with status 'reserved' or 'checked_out', even if their dates are in the past; they are no-shows or completed stays, not overstays.

success_criteria.summary: Expected overstays are seed checked_in reservations with check_out < ep. For each: status='overstay', overstay_days=(ep-check_out).days, run freed, one communications row, one audit_log row. One ops_reports 'boarding_overstay_summary' row per batch with all aggregates. Aggregates are recomputed two independent ways (raw-row Python and SQL JOIN/GROUP BY/SUM) and must agree. No other reservations, runs, or communications are modified.

checks.expect: Expected checked_in reservations with check_out < ep are status='overstay' with correct overstay_days; all other reservations unchanged
Runs for expected overstays are 'available' with current_patient_id cleared; other runs unchanged
One overstay email per expected overstay with exact subject and (patient_id, reservation_id) keys
One OVERSTAY_FLAGGED entry per expected overstay
Exactly one boarding_overstay_summary row per batch with correct aggregates
overstay_count and total_overstay_days agree between raw-row Python and SQL SUM/COUNT; by_run_type/by_location/by_species agree between raw-row Python and SQL GROUP BY

hazards: Status filter: at the default episode date 2026-09-30 the snapshot has 5 checked_in reservations (ids 1-5) with check_out strictly before the episode. There are reserved reservations with dates in the past (e.g., id 8 check_out 2026-09-28, id 7 check_out 2026-09-30) and 113 checked_out reservations; a solution that flags any reservation with check_out < ep as overstay over-flags.

Strict boundary: reservation 7 has check_out exactly 2026-09-30, the default episode date. Because the overstay test is check_out < episode_date (strict), reservation 7 is an active reserved guest, not an overstay.

Run freeing with future reservations: the runs for overstays (1-5) also have future reserved bookings (99 on run 3, 98 on run 4). The agent must free the run to 'available' but must NOT delete or modify those reserved reservations.
overstay_days is a whole-day date difference, not a timestamp diff. At default ep, reservation 1 is 21 days overdue and reservations 2/3/4 are 24 days overdue.
Owner notification must come from the patient record and be sent once per (patient, reservation), not once per owner or once per run.
Idempotency: a second run must not duplicate communications, audit_log, or ops_reports rows, and overstay_days must be the same.

uniqueness_report.differentiation_note: Upgraded from a simple overstay flag to a full closeout workflow: status + overstay_days, run freeing, owner notification, audit trail, and a multi-dimensional summary. The mission explicitly excludes no-shows and future reserved decoys and verifies every aggregate via independent SQL.
